column1: # The patch revisions that changed what a match computes (the simulation),
# oldest first. A game plays a replay only when every game of its recording
# was of the last one's revision or later: a recording of older games plays
# out otherwise in a newer one (session::v026g::replays, read at build time;
# A PR whose change makes a match play out otherwise (an exe patch of the
# game's rules, what a kit or a respawn is, ...) adds the row
# at the end: a PR never knows its revision. The release that ships it is
# that revision: its server takes `next` for its SRP_MIN_PATCH_REVISION
# (the release's own, set at its swap), and release/release.sh writes the
# number in place of `next` in its record. One `next` row at most: a second
# simulation change before the release adds its words to that row.
